sections.title: How do I report the status of the ballast tank?

sections.title: What is the maximum loading rate?

sections.title: What should I do if I detect a leak at the manifold connection?

sections.title: What should I do if there is a toxic spillage on board?
sections.text:
Q: What should I do if there is a toxic spillage on board?
A: A vessel is dealing with a toxic spillage and potential fire emergency. First, take actions according to the Emergency Plan; Then, turn the vessel out of the wind; Next, put on protective clothing and breathing apparatus; After that, stop the spillage; Finally, let the spillage evaporate; Then, remove the spillage with synthetic scoops; Then, use absorbents for the spillage; Then, do not touch the spillage; Then, separate contaminated goods from other goods; Then, cover contaminated goods with tarpaulins; Then, only open the container when smoking is stopped; Then, cool down the container with water; Then, ventilate the hold(s) carefully; Then, close the hatch and operate the fire extinguishing system; Then, fight the fire from a great distance; Then, flood the hold(s); Then, rescue persons; Then, take injured persons to a safe area; Then, provide first aid to injured persons; Then, call the ambulance; Then, take off and dispose contaminated clothing; Then, alter course for the nearest port and inform on radio. sections.title: What checks need to be done before loading the reefer holds?

sections.title: what should passengers do in case of an emergency?

sections.title: What is the role of a Rescue Co-ordination Centre?

Q: Regarding Channel 08: What should I do if I accidentally activate my EPIRB And in the context of marine_vhf_radio_sample_pages — How do I initiate a VHF call to another vessel? Please explain what each source says and combine into one recommendation.
A: According to Ship radio information ofcom.pdf (Ship Radio Information): The excerpt provides guidelines for using VHF marine radio channels, particularly in distress situations. The steps are: make your initial distress call on Channel 16; then use Channel 13 or primary inter-ship channels if no response is received; then contact the Coastguard immediately if you accidentally activate an EPIRB/PLB. Use 16, 13, 06, 08, 72, 77. Use the prowords MAYDAY, OVER. Channel 16 is the primary distress channel monitored by the UK Coastguard.

According to marine_vhf_radio_sample_pages.pdf (66 Marine VHF Radio Handbook Chapter 4): A yacht named Neptune is attempting to contact an oil tanker named Marbella during an Atlantic crossing. The steps are: contact the tanker on channel 16; then identify yourself and your vessel; then wait for the tanker to respond; then confirm the change of channel when requested. Use 16, 08. Use the prowords OVER, OUT, THIS IS, SAY AGAIN. Channel 16 is used for initial contact and distress calls.

Combined recommendation on Channel 08: Channel 16 is the primary distress channel monitored by the UK Coastguard. EPIRB/PLB devices must be properly stowed to avoid accidental activation. Channel 16 is used for initial contact and distress calls. The yacht must identify itself with its name and call sign.

The steps are: register all EPIRBs and PLBs with the MCA; then notify MCA EPIRB Registry of any acquisition or transfer of 406 MHz EPIRB or PLB; then advise Ofcom of any changes regarding EPIRBs or PLBs; then register 1.6 GHz EPIRBs with Inmarsat CAG.
